metadata.title: West Bengal Soils - Part 3: Old Alluvial Plains (Rarh) and New Alluvial Plains
metadata.region_covered: Birbhum, Burdwan, Murshidabad, Hooghly, Nadia, North 24 Parganas, Maldah
metadata.source: National Bureau of Soil Survey and Land Use Planning (ICAR), Nagpur
metadata.note: These are the most extensive and agriculturally important soils of West Bengal

properties.soil_name: Red and laterite soils, Old alluvial soils
properties.texture_detailed: Loam, Sandy clay loam, Clay loam
properties.slope: Nearly level to very gently sloping (0-3%)
properties.slope_class: Nearly level to very gently sloping plains
properties.limitations: Moderate fertility, Seasonal moisture stress, Moderate acidity
properties.management_practices: Balanced fertilization, Organic matter addition, Crop rotation, Supplemental irrigation
properties.description: Very deep, moderately well to well drained, fine loamy soils on nearly level to very gently sloping plains. These old alluvial soils are moderately productive and extensively cultivated with rice-based cropping systems.

properties.soil_name: Red and laterite soils, Acidic old alluvial soils
properties.land_capability: Class II-III (Good land with acid limitation)
properties.irrigation_suitability: Suitable - irrigation needed in dry season
properties.limitations: Strong acidity, Low phosphorus, Moderate fertility, Aluminium toxicity risk
properties.management_practices: Liming (critical), Phosphate fertilization, Organic manuring, Green manuring, Integrated nutrient management
properties.productivity_rating: Medium (high with proper lime and fertilizer management)
properties.description: Very deep, moderately drained, fine loamy soils on nearly level plains; strongly acid reaction. These soils represent the largest soil area in West Bengal and are extensively cultivated but require lime application for optimal productivity.

properties.region: Rarh Plains - Lower Alluvial with Drainage Impairment
properties.soil_name: Grey to brown alluvial soils, Hydromorphic soils
properties.usda_classification: Fine to Very Fine Loamy, Typic Ochraqualfs
properties.texture_detailed: Silt loam, Silty clay loam, Clay loam
properties.drainage: Somewhat poorly to moderately well drained
properties.slope_class: Nearly level plains with poor drainage
properties.rooting_depth: Moderate to deep (70-120cm, may be restricted by poor drainage)
properties.land_capability: Class II-III (Good for rice, limitations for upland crops)
properties.limitations: Seasonal waterlogging, Moderate to strong acidity, Poor drainage, Limited aeration in wet season
properties.management_practices: Improved drainage, Raised bed cultivation for dry crops, Timely transplanting of rice, Zinc and sulphur application
properties.productivity_rating: High for wetland rice, Medium for upland crops
properties.description: Very deep, somewhat poorly to moderately well drained, fine to very fine loamy soils on nearly level plains; strongly acid to neutral reaction. These are the most extensive soils in West Bengal, ideal for wetland rice cultivation but requiring drainage management for dry season crops.

properties.texture_detailed: Sandy loam, Loamy sand, Fine sandy loam
properties.slope: Nearly level to very gently sloping (0-2%)
properties.slope_class: Nearly level to very gently sloping plains
properties.land_capability: Class III (Good land with moisture and fertility limitations)
properties.irrigation_suitability: Highly suitable - essential for crop production
properties.limitations: Low water holding capacity, Low fertility, Acidity, Drought proneness, Low organic matter
properties.management_practices: Frequent irrigation, Heavy organic manuring, Balanced fertilization, Mulching, Green manuring
properties.productivity_rating: Medium to high (with irrigation and fertilizers)
properties.description: Very deep, moderately well drained, coarse loamy soils on nearly level to very gently sloping plains; strongly to slightly acidic reaction. These light-textured soils are excellent for potato and vegetable cultivation with proper irrigation management.

properties.soil_name: Brown to grey alluvial soils, Recent levee soils
properties.texture_detailed: Loam, Silt loam, Sandy clay loam
properties.parent_material: Recent alluvium from Ganga and tributaries
properties.slope: Nearly level to very gently sloping (0-2%)
properties.slope_class: Nearly level to very gently sloping flood plains (natural levees)
properties.land_use: Paddy, Wheat, Jute, Sugarcane, Vegetables, Pulses
properties.limitations: Occasional flooding, Variable fertility due to recent deposition
properties.management_practices: Balanced fertilization, Crop rotation, Timely sowing, Flood management
properties.description: Very deep, moderately well drained, fine loamy soils on nearly level to very gently sloping flood plains; slightly acidic to slightly alkaline reaction. These are among the most fertile and productive soils in West Bengal, suitable for intensive multi-cropping systems.

properties.usda_classification: Fine Loamy to Fine, Typic Ustifluvents
properties.texture_detailed: Silty clay loam, Clay loam, Silty clay
properties.rooting_depth: Moderate to deep (80-130cm, may be restricted by poor drainage)
properties.land_capability: Class I-II (Excellent for rice, good for other crops with drainage)
properties.irrigation_suitability: Suitable - may need drainage in wet season
properties.limitations: Seasonal waterlogging, Poor drainage in monsoon, Limited aeration
properties.management_practices: Improved drainage, Timely transplanting, Raised bed cultivation for rabi crops, Zinc and boron application
properties.productivity_rating: Very high for rice, Medium to high for upland crops
properties.description: Very deep, somewhat poorly drained, fine loamy to fine soils on nearly level flood plains; slightly acidic to slightly alkaline reaction. These are highly productive soils for wetland rice but require drainage improvement for successful dry season cropping.

properties.region: Gangetic New Alluvial Plains - Low-lying Areas
properties.soil_name: Grey to dark grey clayey soils, Low-lying basin soils
properties.parent_material: Fine-textured recent alluvium with poor drainage
properties.slope_class: Nearly level to depressional flood plains
properties.rooting_depth: Moderate (60-100cm, restricted by poor drainage and heavy texture)
properties.land_use: Paddy (single to double cropping), Limited dry season crops
properties.land_capability: Class II-III (Excellent for rice, limited for upland crops)
properties.irrigation_suitability: Not needed for kharif, drainage needed for rabi
properties.limitations: Poor drainage, Heavy texture, Slow permeability, Prolonged waterlogging, Difficult tillage when dry
properties.management_practices: Drainage improvement critical, Suitable for wetland rice only, Green manuring, Early transplanting
properties.productivity_rating: Very high for wetland rice, Low for dry season crops
properties.description: Very deep, somewhat poorly to poorly drained, fine (clayey) soils on nearly level to depressional flood plains; slightly acidic to slightly alkaline reaction. These soils are best suited for wetland rice cultivation and are difficult to manage for dry season crops without extensive drainage.
